root_cause.text: In `x509_process_extension`, the code reads `v[0]` to verify the ASN.1 tag before checking that `vlen` is sufficient, causing an out-of-bounds read when parsing empty or truncated Basic Constraints or Key Usage extensions.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states "first byte of the extension is read before checking its length." The patch moves the `if (vlen < 4)` (Key Usage) and `if (vlen < 2)` (Basic Constraints) checks before the `if (v[0] != ...)` checks, confirming the length validation was performed after the out-of-bounds read.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The commit message states "first byte of the extension is read before checking its length." candidates.rationale: Reads v[0] before checking that vlen is sufficient, causing out-of-bounds read when vlen < 1.
Length check is placed after the vulnerable read of v[0]; its late position is part of the vulnerability pattern.
Reads v[0] before verifying vlen is at least 1, allowing out-of-bounds read on truncated extension.
Length check occurs after the tag check; its ordering is a key factor in the vulnerability.
Reads v[1] after the length check, but still part of the extension parsing sequence that could be affected by earlier OOB read.

vuln_statements.explanation: Reads v[0] before checking that vlen is sufficient, causing out-of-bounds read when vlen < 1. This is the primary vulnerable access for Basic Constraints extension.
Reads v[0] before verifying vlen is at least 1, allowing out-of-bounds read on truncated Key Usage extension.
Length check placed after the vulnerable read of v[0]; its late position means the out-of-bounds read has already occurred, failing to prevent the vulnerability.
Length check occurs after the tag check (v[0] read); its ordering is a key factor in the vulnerability as it does not prevent the earlier out-of-bounds access.

Reads v[1] after a length check (vlen < 2), but this check might be insufficient if vlen is exactly 2? Actually vlen < 2 ensures vlen >=2 for this read, but the earlier v[0] read already caused OOB if vlen was 0. Still part of the extension parsing sequence, potentially affected if vlen was 1 (but then length check fails). Included as part of the overall vulnerable pattern.
